mainTopic: Hanging flesh and limbs (מדולדלין) of an animal: whether the animal's own blood at שחיטה makes them able to become טמא (הכשר), what happens when the animal dies, and the גמרא's opening question about why the hanging limb has only טומאת אוכלין.
overview: The משנה finishes its rules about flesh and a limb hanging from an animal. If the animal is slaughtered, רבי מאיר says the שחיטה blood prepares the hanging pieces for טומאה, and רבי שמעון disagrees. If the animal dies, the flesh still needs הכשר. רבי מאיר says the limb gives טומאה as אבר מן החי, not as אבר נבלה, and רבי שמעון says it is טהור. The גמרא asks why a hanging limb gets only טומאת אוכלין. It answers that the limb cannot heal, so it counts as food, but נבלה needs the limb to actually fall off ('כי יפול'), and a ברייתא confirms this. This split supports שמואל, who says figs that dried on the tree count as picked for טומאה but as attached for שבת. One attempted proof for שמואל is rejected, and a challenge from a ברייתא about a broken branch is answered. Finally the גמרא asks what רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון disagree about. רבה says it is whether the animal is a 'handle' (יד) for the limb. אביי says it is whether a weakly attached piece counts as one with the whole, and רבי יוחנן's contradiction in רבי מאיר's words begins to show he agrees with אביי. That contradiction continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When the animal is slaughtered, does its own blood prepare the hanging pieces?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the blood of the שחיטה makes the hanging flesh and limb able to become טמא. רבי שמעון says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the animal was slaughtered, the hanging pieces become ready to receive טומאה through its blood, says רבי מאיר. רבי שמעון says they do not become ready.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה deals with an animal that had flesh or a limb hanging from it and was then slaughtered. It asks whether the blood that comes out at the שחיטה counts as the liquid that 'prepares' those pieces for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא after a liquid such as blood has touched it. This is called הכשר. רבי מאיר says the שחיטה blood also prepares the hanging pieces. רבי שמעון says it does not prepare them, so they would need some other liquid. The reason for this argument is explained in steps 17 and 18.

keyTerms.meaning: was slaughtered (by proper שחיטה)
they became 'prepared,' meaning able to receive טומאה
the step of food being wet by one of the special liquids so it can become טמא
its blood

phrases.english: If the animal was slaughtered,
they became susceptible [to impurity] through its blood,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the hanging flesh and limb from earlier in the משנה.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Shimon says: they did not become susceptible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier משנה about flesh and limbs hanging from a living animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the שחיטה blood does הכשר for the hanging pieces. רבי שמעון: it does not.

steps.title: When the animal dies, what is the status of the hanging flesh and limb?
steps.stepSummary: If the animal died without שחיטה, the hanging flesh still needs הכשר. רבי מאיר says the limb gives טומאה as an אבר מן החי but not as an אבר נבלה. רבי שמעון says the limb is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the animal died, the hanging flesh needs הכשר. The hanging limb gives טומאה because of 'limb from a living animal,' not because of 'limb of a נבלה.' This is רבי מאיר's view, and רבי שמעון says it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the משנה looks at the case where the animal died instead of being slaughtered. It rules on the hanging flesh and the hanging limb separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hanging flesh does not turn into נבלה flesh when the animal dies. It is treated like ordinary food, so it still needs הכשר before it can become טמא. רבי מאיר says the limb was already considered cut off while the animal was alive, so its טומאה comes from אבר מן החי. רבי שמעון rules the limb טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: died (without שחיטה)
a limb cut from a living animal, which gives טומאה like a נבלה
a limb of an animal that died without שחיטה
rules it טהור (pure)

steps.confusionAlert: Both אבר מן החי and אבר נבלה give טומאה. The argument here is about which category the limb's טומאה comes from, and רבי שמעון says it has neither.

phrases.english: If the animal died,
the flesh requires being made susceptible,

phrases.aramaic: הָאֵבֶר מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי,
phrases.english: the limb imparts impurity as a limb from a living animal,
and it does not impart impurity as a limb of a carcass,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir,
and Rabbi Shimon declares it pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the slaughtered-animal case to the case where the animal died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hanging flesh still needs הכשר. רבי מאיר: the limb is טמא as אבר מן החי, not as אבר נבלה. רבי שמעון: the limb is טהור.
steps.whatToRemember: Death does not turn hanging flesh into נבלה. רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון disagree about whether the limb gives טומאה at all.

steps.title: The גמרא reads the משנה: food impurity only, not נבלה impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the hanging limb gets טומאת אוכלין but not טומאת נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Food impurity, yes. Carcass impurity, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by drawing an inference from the משנה's earlier ruling that a hanging limb on a living animal becomes טמא as food. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying 'טומאת אוכלין,' the משנה implies that the limb does not have the stronger טומאת נבלה. That stronger kind would make people and utensils טמא too. The גמרא spells out this limit so it can question it.

keyTerms.meaning: the discussion of the משנה
the impurity of ordinary food, which is a weaker kind
the impurity of an unslaughtered carcass, which is stronger and can make people טמא
yes

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Impurity of food, yes,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier ruling in the משנה about a limb hanging from a living animal.

phrases.english: impurity of a carcass, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין – אִין, טוּמְאַת נְבֵלָה – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by going back to the earlier part of the משנה about a hanging limb.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hanging limb has טומאת אוכלין only, not טומאת נבלה.

steps.title: Either the limb can heal or it cannot, so the middle status makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case this is. If the limb can heal, it should not be טמא even as food. If it cannot heal, it should be טמא as נבלה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it can heal, it should not even become impure as food. If it cannot heal, it should also become impure as a carcass!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the in-between status it just pointed out. It shows that neither possible case fits the משנה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the limb can heal, it is still a living part of the animal, so it should not count as food at all. If it cannot heal, it is like a dead limb and should carry full טומאת נבלה. A ruling of 'food impurity only' seems to fit neither case.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? How exactly are we picturing it?
it can heal and reattach
also, even

steps.whyThisMatters: This question frames the rest of the סוגיא. The answer has to explain how a limb can be 'dead enough' to be food but not dead enough to be נבלה.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If they can heal,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין נָמֵי לָא לִיטַּמּוּ,
phrases.english: they should not become impure even with food impurity,
and if they cannot heal,
they should become impure with carcass impurity as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference made in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a hanging limb has טומאת אוכלין but not טומאת נבלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided question: if the limb can heal it is fully alive and not food, and if it cannot heal it is fully dead and נבלה. Neither side leaves room for a middle status.

steps.title: The case is a limb that cannot heal, and נבלה needs the limb to fall off
steps.stepSummary: The limb cannot heal, so it counts as food. But טומאת נבלה is different: the פסוק 'כי יפול' requires the limb to actually fall off.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the case is where the limb cannot heal. But טומאת נבלה is different, because the Torah says 'if it falls.' It is not נבלה until it actually falls off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4. It picks the 'cannot heal' side and explains why the limb is still not טמא as נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the limb cannot heal, it is treated as already cut off, so it can become טמא as food. טומאת נבלה has its own rule from the פסוק: the limb must physically fall off the animal. Hanging by a thread is not enough for נבלה, even though it is enough for food.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. Opens an answer that keeps one side of the question.
They cannot heal. The limb will never reattach.
It is different.
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah.
Not until it falls off.

steps.confusionAlert: The same limb is treated as cut off for one law (טומאת אוכלין) and as still attached for another (טומאת נבלה). That is not a contradiction. Each law has its own standard.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main idea of the rest of the section. One object can count as attached for some laws and detached for others.

phrases.english: Really, it is a case where they cannot heal,
and the impurity of a carcass is different,
for the Merciful One said: "if it falls"
meaning, not until it actually falls off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 4 by picking the 'cannot heal' side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the question and adds a special rule from a פסוק for נבלה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the limb cannot heal, it should be נבלה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: It cannot heal, so it counts as food. But נבלה needs the limb to actually fall off, as the פסוק 'כי יפול' says.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a limb hanging by a hair is not נבלה, because of 'יפול'. Even so, it can become טמא as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. A limb or flesh hanging from an animal, attached by a thread as thin as a hair: you might think it gives טומאת נבלה. So the פסוק says 'falls,' meaning not until it falls off. Even so, it can become טמא as food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what step 5 said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same word 'יפול' to rule out טומאת נבלה for a limb that is still hanging. It also states openly that the limb still gets טומאת אוכלין. That is the exact split the משנה needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Hanging loosely, partly cut off.
Still attached.
A thread as thin as a hair.
You might think. This sets up a wrong idea that the פסוק will reject.
So the פסוק says. It brings the source that rejects the wrong idea.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
The limb and the flesh that are hanging from an animal
and are attached by a thread as thin as a hair,
you might think they give the impurity of a carcass?
So the verse says "falls," meaning not until it falls off,
and even so, they become impure as food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 5 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that a limb that cannot heal gets טומאת אוכלין but not טומאת נבלה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads 'יפול' as 'until it falls off' and still gives the limb טומאת אוכלין.
steps.whatToRemember: A limb hanging by a thread is not נבלה, because it has not fallen off. It can still become טמא as food.

steps.title: This supports שמואל's rule about figs that dried on the tree
steps.stepSummary: The same split supports רב חייא בר אשי in the name of שמואל. Figs that dried on the tree count as picked for טומאת אוכלין, but count as attached for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב חייא בר אשי, who said in the name of שמואל: figs that dried up on their tree can become טמא as food. And someone who picks them on שבת must bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the ברייתא it just brought supports another אמורא. That אמורא also treats one object as attached for one law and detached for another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Figs that dried on the tree are like they were already picked, so they get טומאת אוכלין. But they are still physically attached, so picking them on שבת counts as picking. The hanging limb works the same way: detached for food טומאה, attached for נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: It supports him.
Dried up and shriveled.
Their tree or plant, the thing they grow on.
Picks or pulls something off where it grows.
Must bring a sin-offering, for doing a מלאכה on שבת by mistake.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: This supports Rav Chiya bar Ashi,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: for Rav Chiya bar Ashi said in the name of Shmuel:
Figs that dried up while still on their tree
can become impure as food,
and one who picks them on Shabbat must bring a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 6 to support a related rule of שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that figs dried on the tree are detached for טומאת אוכלין but attached for שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in step 6, where a hanging limb is detached for food טומאה but not detached for נבלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Figs that dried on the tree can become טמא as food, and picking them on שבת makes one חייב חטאת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the hanging-limb case into a wider idea. Something can count as detached for one law and attached for another.

steps.title: Trying to support שמואל from vegetables that dried on the plant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a ברייתא may support שמואל. Vegetables like cabbage and gourd that dried on the plant cannot become טמא as food. If they were cut and then dried, they can.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? Vegetables that dried up on their plant, like cabbage and gourd, cannot become טמא as food. If he cut them and dried them, they can become טמא as food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests another source that might support שמואל. The word 'לימא' shows this is only a suggestion, and the גמרא will test it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested support seems to be this: these vegetables are not טמא as food only because they become hard and are no longer food. If so, a dried-on-the-plant item that is still food, like a fig, would count as picked. That is שמואל's view. Because the גמרא opens with 'לימא', this reading may still be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It opens a suggested proof that is often rejected afterward.
Vegetables.
Cabbage.
Gourd.
He cut them off and then dried them.

steps.confusionAlert: 'לימא מסייע ליה' does not mean the proof works. It is a suggestion the גמרא is about to check.

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him?
Vegetables that dried up while still on their plant,
such as cabbage and gourd,
cannot become impure as food;
if he cut them off and then dried them,
they can become impure as food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a second source that might support שמואל's rule from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that produce dried on the plant counts as picked for טומאת אוכלין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about cabbage and gourd that dried on the plant compared with ones cut and then dried.

steps.title: Cut and dried vegetables are just wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second half of the ברייתא. Cut and fully dried cabbage or gourd is like wood, so how could it become טמא as food?
steps.simpleTranslation: Could you really think that if he cut them and dried them, they can become טמא as food? It is just wood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא from Step 8, which said that vegetables that were cut and then dried can become טמא as food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dried cabbage and gourd are not food at all. Only food can get טומאת אוכלין. So it makes no sense that cutting them before they dried would make them טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (a strong 'that can't be right')
He cut them and dried them
Mere wood, meaning not food at all

phrases.english: He cut them and dried them, does that enter your mind?!
phrases.notes: This is quoting the ברייתא from Step 8, which said these can become טמא.

phrases.english: It is merely wood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא quoted in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that cut and dried vegetables can become טמא as food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dried cabbage and gourd are not edible, and only edible things get טומאת אוכלין

steps.title: They were cut in order to be dried
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that the ברייתא means they were cut while still moist, in order to dry them later. While they are still moist, they can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: The case is where he cut them in order to dry them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא differently. They are not dried yet. They were only cut with a plan to dry them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that a plan to dry them does not take away their food status yet. As long as they are still moist and edible, they can still become טמא as food.

keyTerms.meaning: With the intention of / in order to
To dry them

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
It is where he cut them in order to dry them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא spoke of vegetables already cut and fully dried
steps.terutzMaskana: They were cut while moist, intending to dry them, and are still food for now

steps.title: Inference: other dried fruits can become טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the ברייתא that only cabbage and gourd lose food status when they dry on the plant. Other fruits that dried on the plant can still become טמא as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that it is cabbage and gourd, which are not edible once dried. But other fruits can become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof for שמואל. It draws a careful inference from the first half of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cabbage and gourd are not טמא only because drying makes them inedible. That means other fruits, which are still edible when dried, can become טמא as food even though they dried on the plant. Next the גמרא will ask exactly what case this is.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason (often used to set up an inference)
Cabbage and gourd
Fit to be eaten
Other kinds of produce

phrases.english: The reason is that it is cabbage and gourd,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּיִבְּשָׁן לָאו בְּנֵי אֲכִילָה נִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: since once he dried them they are not edible,
but other produce does become טמא.
phrases.notes: This means other fruits that dried while still on the plant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the attempted proof for שמואל from Step 8, now that the ברייתא's wording is clear
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that fruit dried on the tree counts as picked for טומאת אוכלין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first half of the ברייתא about cabbage and gourd, read for its implication

steps.title: The case must be without the stems drying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the inference is about. If the stems dried too, the ruling would be obvious. So it must be a case where only the fruit dried, which supports שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If the fruit and its stems both dried, that is obvious! Rather, isn't it a case where it dried without its stems?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof for שמואל by pinning down the exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stems also dried, the fruit is clearly cut off from the plant, so a ברייתא would not need to teach it. So the case must be fruit that dried while its stems stayed moist. Even so, it counts as picked for טומאה, just as שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
Their stems
It is obvious (so why teach it?)
Rather, isn't it...? (leads into the proof)

steps.confusionAlert: In this case the fruit itself is dried, but its stems are still moist and connected to the plant. That is why it can count as attached for שבת but picked for טומאה.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If they dried, both the fruit and its stems, that is obvious!
Rather, isn't it where they dried without their stems?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof started in Step 11
steps.raayaObject: שמואל: dried fruit counts as picked for טומאת אוכלין even though it counts as attached for שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's implication, read as fruit that dried while its stems stayed moist

steps.title: The stems dried too; the line sets up the next case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The case really is where the fruit and the stems both dried. That obvious case was taught only to contrast with the next case, cutting in order to dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is where the fruit and its stems dried. It was needed for the case where he cut them in order to dry them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says the ברייתא does not have to be about moist stems, so it gives no proof for שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case may be obvious, but the ברייתא said it anyway to set up the second case: cut while moist in order to dry, and still טמא for now. Since the case can be one where the stems dried, nothing here shows שמואל's split between שבת and טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth (leads into the rejection)
It was needed for him (to teach)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about cabbage and gourd does not prove שמואל. It can be read as a case where the stems dried too, and the obvious first case was taught only to set up the case of cutting in order to dry.

phrases.english: Actually, it is where the fruit and its stems both dried,

phrases.aramaic: וּקְצָצָן עַל מְנָת לְיַבְּשָׁן אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and it was needed for the case of cutting them in order to dry them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for שמואל built in Steps 11 and 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from this ברייתא is rejected. שמואל's rule itself is not refuted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the obvious case would never be taught. But a ברייתא can teach an obvious case to set up the next one.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a broken branch challenges שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. Fruit on a branch that broke off counts as detached, and fruit that dried on the tree counts as attached. The גמרא suggests that both rules apply to all matters, which would go against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if a tree's branch broke off and it has fruit on it, the fruit counts as detached. If the fruit dried on the tree, it counts as attached. Doesn't this mean that just as 'detached' applies to everything, 'attached' also applies to everything?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say dried fruit on a tree counts as attached in every way, even for טומאה. That would contradict שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל held that fruit which dried on the plant can still become טמא as food, as if it were detached. The ברייתא calls dried fruit 'like attached.' The גמרא reasons that the two halves of the ברייתא should match: since the first half clearly means 'detached for everything,' the second half should mean 'attached for everything,' which would include טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: broke off (a branch split off from the tree)
detached from the ground or plant
attached to the ground or plant
'Isn't it that…?' — the גמרא offers a reading it thinks is correct
for all their matters, meaning in every area of הלכה

phrases.english: Come and hear: a tree from which a branch broke off
and there is fruit on it, the fruit is like detached,
if the fruit dried, it is like attached.
Isn't it that:
just as 'detached' applies to all matters,
phrases.notes: 'All matters' means both the laws of שבת and the laws of טומאה.

phrases.english: so too 'attached' applies to all matters?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for שמואל was rejected, the גמרא now tries a source that goes against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that fruit which dried on the plant can still become טמא as food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both halves of the ברייתא should work the same way. If 'detached' covers every area of הלכה, then 'attached' should too, including טומאה.

steps.title: Each half of the ברייתא follows its own rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. Each case in the ברייתא is understood on its own terms. Dried fruit can count as attached for שבת but as detached for טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the cases really the same? This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge. It says we do not have to read both halves of the ברייתא the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fruit on the broken branch is detached in every way. The fruit that dried on the tree is called 'attached' only for some laws, such as שבת. For טומאה it can still be treated as detached, so שמואל stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Are they comparable?' — a way of rejecting a comparison between two cases
this one is as it is, and that one is as it is; each case has its own rule

phrases.english: Are the cases comparable?
This is as it is, and that is as it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge to שמואל from step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that both clauses of the ברייתא must apply equally to all areas of הלכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge wrongly matched the two clauses. Dried fruit can be attached for שבת and still detached for טומאה.
steps.whatToRemember: Fruit that dried on the tree may be 'attached' for one area of הלכה and 'detached' for another, so שמואל's view survives.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that 'like attached' means attached for every law. Here it is limited, and טומאה is treated differently.

steps.title: What do רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון disagree about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of a slaughtered animal. It asks what principle underlies the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If the animal was slaughtered…' What are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next case. It asks for the reason behind the argument, which sets up רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר says the blood of the slaughtering makes the hanging limb ready to become טמא, and רבי שמעון says it does not. The גמרא wants to know what basic idea causes them to rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: the animal was slaughtered — the opening words of the case in the משנה
about what are they arguing? — asking for the root of a dispute

phrases.english: The animal was slaughtered, etc.
phrases.notes: וכו׳ means 'and so on.' The גמרא quotes only the first words of the משנה's case.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of dried fruit back to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון about the slaughtered animal.

steps.title: רבה: is the animal a 'handle' for its limb?
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that they disagree about whether the animal's body counts as a יד (handle) for the limb hanging from it. If it does, the slaughtering blood touching the body also makes the limb ready to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: they disagree about whether an animal serves as a handle for its limb. One holds that the animal is not a handle for the limb, and the other holds that the animal is a handle for the limb.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question by naming the principle the two תנאים disagree about. They argue over whether the animal's body is a 'handle' for its partly cut limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that when a handle is made ready to become טמא, the food attached to it is made ready too. The blood touched the body, not the limb. רבי מאיר says the body is a handle for the limb, so the limb is made ready. רבי שמעון says it is not, so the limb is not made ready.

keyTerms.meaning: a handle; something attached to food that is treated as part of it for טומאה
a limb (here, a limb partly cut off and hanging from the animal)
one master holds — a way of presenting each side of a dispute

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of יד, a handle that brings the food along with it for טומאה, is the key that explains the whole dispute in the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbah said:
They disagree about whether an animal becomes a handle for the limb:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר אֵין בְּהֵמָה נַעֲשֵׂית יָד לְאֵבֶר,
phrases.english: One master holds an animal does not become a handle for the limb,
phrases.notes: This first view is רבי שמעון's, and the second one is רבי מאיר's.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר בְּהֵמָה נַעֲשֵׂית יָד לְאֵבֶר.
phrases.english: and the other master holds an animal does become a handle for the limb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about whether an animal counts as a יד (handle) for its limb. רבי מאיר says yes, and רבי שמעון says no.

steps.title: אביי's explanation: is a weakly attached piece still part of the whole?
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the dispute is about a small part that is only weakly attached. If you lift it, the large part does not come up with it. רבי מאיר holds it still counts as one with the large part. רבי שמעון holds it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They disagree about a case where you grab the small part and the large part does not come up with it. One Sage holds that it still counts as one with the large part. The other Sage holds that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second answer to the question from step 16 about why רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון disagree. He offers a different principle from the one רבה gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, the question was whether the animal works as a 'handle' for the limb. אביי moves the question somewhere else: is a limb that hangs on so weakly still part of the animal at all? If it is part of the animal (רבי מאיר), then whatever happens to the animal's body also happens to the limb. If it is not (רבי שמעון), the limb is treated as a separate item.

keyTerms.meaning: Grabbing the small part (here, the hanging limb)
And the large part does not come up with it, because the connection is too weak to lift the whole
It is like it, meaning it counts as one item with the large part
They disagree (about this point)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'small' and 'large'. The small part is the hanging limb, and the large part is the animal's body. The case is that lifting the limb does NOT lift the animal, so the connection is weak.
steps.whyThisMatters: Now there are two competing explanations of the משנה, one from רבה and one from אביי. The rest of this section brings support for אביי's reading.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוֹחֵז בְּקָטָן וְאֵין גָּדוֹל עוֹלֶה עִמּוֹ
phrases.english: In a case where one grabs the small part and the large part does not come up with it
phrases.notes: The small part is the hanging limb, and the large part is the animal's body.

phrases.english: is where they disagree.
One Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This first Sage is רבי מאיר, and the other one is רבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹחֵז בְּקָטָן וְאֵין גָּדוֹל עוֹלֶה עִמּוֹ –
phrases.english: When one grabs the small part and the large part does not come up with it,
it still counts as one with it,
and the other Sage holds: it does not count as one with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: בְּאוֹחֵז בְּקָטָן וְאֵין גָּדוֹל עוֹלֶה עִמּוֹ קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question in step 16. It stands as an alternative to רבה's answer in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about whether a weakly attached piece, one that does not lift the whole when it is lifted, still counts as part of the whole. רבי מאיר says yes and רבי שמעון says no.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן also explains the dispute this way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רבי יוחנן also held that רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון disagree about the weakly attached piece, just as אביי said.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן also holds that they disagree about a case where one grabs the small part and the large part does not come up with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא claims that אביי's explanation matches what רבי יוחנן thought. This line sets up the next step, where the גמרא will show the source for this claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is support for אביי, not a new rule. It shows that his reading of the משנה goes back to an earlier and greater authority, רבי יוחנן. The proof comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: And also, meaning this person agrees too
Holds, is of the opinion
They disagree

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan also holds

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוֹחֵז בְּקָטָן וְאֵין גָּדוֹל עוֹלֶה עִמּוֹ
phrases.english: that in a case where one grabs the small part and the large part does not come up with it
is where they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's explanation from step 18 by showing that רבי יוחנן understood the dispute the same way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן also understood the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון to be about a weakly attached piece.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן points out a contradiction in רבי מאיר's words
steps.stepSummary: As proof for step 19, the גמרא quotes רבי יוחנן raising a contradiction between two statements of רבי מאיר. He begins by asking: did רבי מאיר really say that a weakly attached piece counts as one with the whole?
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יוחנן raises a contradiction between one statement of רבי מאיר and another statement of רבי מאיר: Did רבי מאיר really say that when one grabs the small part and the large part does not come up with it, it still counts as one with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי יוחנן read the dispute like אביי did. It quotes the start of a contradiction he found in רבי מאיר's opinions, and the other statement of רבי מאיר is coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's question only makes sense if he understood our משנה the way אביי did: רבי מאיר holds that a weakly attached piece counts as one with the whole. So the very fact that he raised this contradiction shows how he read the משנה. The question 'did רבי מאיר say...?' expresses surprise, because רבי מאיר seems to say the opposite somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a contradiction, literally 'throws' one source against another
One statement of רבי מאיר against another statement of רבי מאיר, a contradiction inside one sage's own words
Did he really say? This shows surprise and opens a challenge

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yochanan raises a contradiction
between a statement of Rabbi Meir and a statement of Rabbi Meir:
Did Rabbi Meir really say

phrases.aramaic: אוֹחֵז בְּקָטָן וְאֵין גָּדוֹל עוֹלֶה עִמּוֹ
phrases.english: that when one grabs the small part and the large part does not come up with it
it still counts as one with it?
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר's view as אביי explained our משנה. The other statement that seems to contradict it comes next.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רָמֵי דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר אַדְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 19. רבי יוחנן's contradiction assumes אביי's reading of רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's view (as אביי reads the משנה) that a weakly attached piece counts as one with the whole
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר seems to say the opposite in another place. That other statement is about to be quoted, so his two statements seem to clash.

steps.title: Opening the contradicting source: a sliced food still partly attached
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא, continuing רבי יוחנן's challenge, begins quoting a source that seems to contradict רבי מאיר's view. The case is food that was cut but stays partly connected.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contrasted it with another source: food that was sliced and is still partly attached.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא starts quoting a second source about a partly attached piece of food, which it will set against רבי מאיר's ruling in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, רבי יוחנן asked whether רבי מאיר really treats a weakly attached piece as one with the whole. Now the גמרא brings a case about the same kind of weak connection: food that was cut but not fully separated. רבי מאיר's ruling there, which comes next, is what will create the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: "And they contrasted them": the גמרא sets one source against another to show they seem to contradict.
Food, here something that can become טמא.
Was sliced or cut.
Still partly attached, connected by only a small part.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect the contradiction to be clear yet. This line only describes the case. You need רבי מאיר's ruling in the next lines to see the clash.

phrases.english: And they contrasted it with another source:
phrases.notes: This continues רבי יוחנן's question from the last step. He is now bringing the second statement of רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: food that was sliced and is partly attached,
phrases.notes: This is from a משנה in מסכת טבול יום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's contradiction from step 20 by beginning to quote the second, conflicting source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר treats a weakly attached piece as one with the whole.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second source about food that is only partly attached will show רבי מאיר ruling in a way that seems to clash with his ruling in our משנה.
